msg: GOAL finalized: 4 kernel optimization methods (3 pure-math baseline + CAKE), 7 hypotheses across 3 phases
design_logic: pure-math baseline first (H1-H3) to remove LLM confounder, then CAKE (H4-H6) to measure LLM marginal contribution, then interpretability (H7)

verdict_reason: kernel manifold (LML-based selection) does NOT improve over fixed Matern-5/2; best_found drops by 0.70 (buchwald) and 0.55 (suzuki); t95 ties on both. Both methods deterministic (std=0) so CI comparison is moot.
note: LML-based kernel selection picks SE*RQ (buchwald) and RQ (suzuki) over Matern-5/2, but these kernels produce WORSE best_found despite higher LML — LML is a model-fit metric, not a downstream-performance metric. This is the classic overfitting-on-model-selection problem.
implication_for_H7: kernel evolution DID select non-Matern kernels (SE*RQ, RQ), confirming data structure is non-Matern. But LML selection is the wrong objective — need acquisition-aware kernel fitness (CAKE uses BIC+acquisition hybrid).

method: gpbo_alas (ALAS learnable alpha-stable kernel, alpha learned from data)
verdict_reason: ALAS learnable alpha-stable kernel performs WORSE than fixed Matern-5/2 on both datasets and both metrics. best_found drops 6.83 (buchwald) and 1.09 (suzuki); t95 explodes 33 and 13 rounds respectively. Alpha learns to ~0.3-0.5 (very rough regime) instead of staying near 2 (Gaussian-like), indicating the powered-exponential parameterization is unstable on one-hot categorical data — alpha=0.3 produces near-singular covariance matrices that destroy GP predictive quality.
note: Same root issue as H1: optimizing the kernel via MLL does not improve downstream BO performance. ALAS alpha collapse to 0.3 suggests MLL is overfitting on the small 35-row prior; the paper validates ALAS on d=3-30 continuous tasks, not high-dimensional one-hot (d=44/107) categorical spaces.
implication_for_H7: ALAS learned alpha=0.3-0.5 (heavily non-Matern), confirming categorical BO data has structure that deviates from Matern-5/2. But like H1, learning it via MLL makes things worse, not better.

method: gpbo_dkl (MLP feature extractor + Matern-5/2 in feature space)
verdict_reason: Mixed results: DKL WINS on buchwald t95 (2 vs 8, faster convergence) but LOSES on best_found (-1.70). On suzuki DKL LOSES on both best_found (-0.32) and t95 (+6). No dataset shows DKL winning on best_found. The t95 win on buchwald is notable but best_found regression is the primary competition metric (50% weight).
note: DKL is the first pure-math method to show ANY improvement (buchwald t95 8→2). The MLP feature extractor learns a representation that enables faster convergence on the smaller (783-point, 4-var) buchwald space, but overfits on the larger (5731-point, 5-var) suzuki space. This is consistent with the DKL paper observation that deep kernels need sufficient data to avoid overfitting; 35 train points is marginal.
implication_for_H7: DKL uses fixed Matern-5/2 in feature space, so it does not directly select a different kernel expression. But the learned MLP features implicitly learn a non-Matern structure.

method: gpbo_cake (LLM-guided kernel evolution via crossover+mutation, BIC fitness)
verdict_reason: Mixed: CAKE WINS on suzuki best_found (98.69 vs 97.29, Δ=+1.40) — first kernel method to beat baseline on best_found. But LOSES on buchwald best_found (-3.50) and t95 on both. LLM consistently selects LIN kernel (linear) across all 8 evolution steps on both datasets, ignoring periodic/RQ structure. The BIC fitness heavily favors LIN because linear kernels have fewer params and the one-hot categorical space is sparse.
note: Notable: CAKE is the FIRST method to beat baseline on best_found in any dataset (suzuki +1.40). But the LLM-BIC loop converges to LIN (simplest kernel) because BIC penalizes complexity. The LLM proposes kernels but BIC rejects them. This suggests BIC alone is the wrong fitness — the CAKE paper uses BIC+acquisition hybrid (BAKER) which we did not implement.
implication_for_H5: CAKE did not definitively beat pure-math methods. H5 (CAKE vs best pure-math) will show CAKE ~ DKL (both inconclusive). The key insight: BIC-only fitness converges to simplest kernel; need acquisition-aware fitness.
implication_for_H7: CAKE selected LIN (not PER/RQ), suggesting LLM+BIC sees linear structure in the one-hot embedding. This is different from H1 (Manifold chose SE*RQ, RQ) — different fitness functions find different structure.

verdict_reason: Same results as pre-fix H4: suzuki best_found WINS (+1.40), buchwald LOSES (-3.50). Fix confirmed working: LLM now generates composite kernels (M3*(SE*LIN), LIN+SE, SE*LIN, M1+LIN*LIN) that enter the population, but BIC still selects LIN as winner because BIC penalizes composite kernel complexity (num_params).
fixes_applied: extra_body: reasoning_effort=low → thinking={type: disabled} (fixes empty content)
max_tokens: 256 → 512 (room for kernel expression after reasoning)
key_finding: LLM IS working now (proposes LIN+SE, SE*LIN, M3*(SE*LIN), M1+LIN*LIN), but BIC fitness rejects them — BIC penalizes the extra parameters of composite kernels. This confirms the CAKE papers BAKER (BIC+acquisition hybrid) insight: BIC alone is insufficient; need acquisition-aware fitness.
implication_for_H5_H6: H5 (CAKE vs best pure-math) will show CAKE ~ DKL (both inconclusive). H6 (CAKE+mean-shift) needs the BAKER fitness improvement to be meaningful.

method: gpbo_cake (ALL FIXES: thinking=disabled, max_tokens=512, longest-match parser, real observations, normalized fitness, output format, temperature=0.7)
verdict_reason: Same results as before. LLM now properly works: generates composite kernels (M3*M5, LIN+M5, LIN+SE, SE*LIN, LIN*SE) that enter population. But BIC still selects LIN as winner because BIC penalizes composite kernel parameters (44-88 extra params per composite vs LIN alone).
fixes_applied: output format: prompt now requires Kernel:/Reasoning:
key_finding: ALL 4 prompt bugs fixed and verified. LLM generates diverse composite kernels. But BIC-only fitness is the fundamental bottleneck — BIC penalizes composite kernel complexity (num_params). Need BAKER (BIC+acquisition hybrid) fitness to let LLM-generated composites win.
implication: The prompt fixes are necessary but not sufficient. The real blocker is BIC-only fitness rejecting composite kernels. This confirms CAKE papers BAKER insight: need acquisition-aware fitness, not just model-fit (BIC).

method: gpbo_cake (ENSEMBLE: population-weighted predict, all kernels contribute)
verdict_reason: Ensemble improved buchwald significantly (best_found 83.10→85.89, +2.80; t95 9→8). But suzuki t95 exploded (6→24) — ensemble prediction on large pool (5731 points) is unstable. best_found unchanged on suzuki (+1.40 vs baseline, same as pre-ensemble).
key_finding: Ensemble predict WORKS for buchwald (smaller pool, 783 points) — population weighting recovers most of the gap to baseline. But FAILS on suzuki (large pool, 5731 points) — the ensemble of 6 GPs over 5731 points produces high variance predictions that hurt t95.
architecture_change: predict() now blends all population kernels via BIC-weighted mixture (law of total variance), instead of using single best kernel. LLM-generated composite kernels (LIN*M5, LIN*SE, RQ+SE, LIN+PER, LIN*PER) now contribute to predictions with non-zero weights.
implication: Ensemble is correct architecture for small pools. For large pools, need to limit ensemble to top-3 kernels by weight, or use single best for predict + ensemble only for acquisition.

method: CAKE ensemble vs best pure-math method per dataset

buchwald_sub4.verdict: TIE — CAKE and best pure-math produce identical results on buchwald

suzuki.verdict: MIXED — CAKE WINS on best_found (+1.72) but LOSES on t95 (+14). CAKE finds higher yield but converges slower.

verdict_reason: CAKE ties with best pure-math on buchwald (both 85.89). On suzuki, CAKE wins on best_found (+1.72 vs DKL) but t95 explodes (+14). No dataset shows CAKE winning on BOTH metrics. CAKE is the ONLY method to beat baseline on suzuki best_found (+1.40), and it also beats the best pure-math (DKL +1.72), but at the cost of t95.
key_finding: LLM marginal contribution: CAKE > best pure-math on suzuki best_found (+1.72), TIE on buchwald. This suggests LLM kernel evolution adds value for discovering high-yield conditions, but hurts convergence speed (t95). The LLM-generated composite kernels (LIN*PER, LIN+PER) explore more broadly, finding higher peaks but taking longer.
implication_for_H6: H6 tests CAKE + mean-shift combination. If CAKE finds high-yield points (good best_found) and mean-shift accelerates convergence (good t95), the combination could win on both metrics.
